title: React: Components, Props, State, Data Flow

scenes.line1: Why does React use one-way data flow?
scenes.line2: How does it help your UI?
scenes.say: Why does React force data to flow in one direction? And how does that make your UI easier to manage?

scenes.label: Component
scenes.sub: Reusable UI block; takes props as input.
scenes.say: A React component is a reusable block of user interface that takes input called props.
Props are read-only and flow from parent to child. State is local and can be changed inside the component.
Here's a component. Props provide the name. State tracks how many times you've clicked.
Data always flows from parent to child using props. State stays local, keeping updates predictable.

scenes.question: Can a child change its own props?
scenes.wrong: Yes, it can update props directly.
scenes.right: No, props are read-only. Only state can be changed locally.
scenes.say: Here's a trap: Can a child component change its own props? No, props are read-only. Only state can be changed locally.
